summary: Red Meadow platform lookout in the Flathead National Forest: dated 1923, a 1921 forest lookout job at the site, abandoned in the 1930s; no source describes what remains.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1930s per firelookout.com. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Abandoned, not Gone, and no source says whether any part of the platform survived.

access.note: On Flathead National Forest land. The Forest Service runs a public campground at Red Meadow Lake whose access opening date varies. No source describes access to the old platform site itself.

events.note: Frank Crause was employed for two months as a forest lookout at Red Meadow, per an October 1921 Columbian item quoted on montanalookouts.weebly.com. The item does not say what kind of post it was or whether it was this platform.
firelookout.com dates the platform tower to 1923. This is two years after the 1921 item; see resolved_conflicts.
Abandoned in the 1930s per firelookout.com; the sources give only the decade, so the year is a placeholder.

evidence.supports: platform tower dated 1923, with a camp at the southwest end of Red Meadow Lake
evidence.quote: 1923: platform tower, camp at southwest end of Red Meadow Lake.

evidence.supports: location about 13 miles west of Polebridge
lookout is in the Flathead National Forest

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives the platform the status Abandoned
campground at Red Meadow Lake at 5,500 feet with three campsites and picnic day-use areas
evidence.quote: At an elevation of 5,500 feet, Red Meadow Campground has 3 campsites and 3 picnic table day-use areas near Red Meadow Lake.

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives this platform the status Abandoned, and firelookout.com says only that it was abandoned in the 1930s. Neither source says the structure was removed, so Gone is not supported.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com dates the platform tower to 1923. A 1921 Columbian item quoted on montanalookouts.weebly.com says a forest lookout was employed at Red Meadow that year. The item does not say whether it was the same structure, so both dates are kept: staffing from 1921 and the platform from 1923.

sources.title: Red Meadow Lake Campground
sources.publisher: Flathead National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Thin record: four sources, and the Firelookout.com page has one line of detail. The 1921 forest lookout job and the 1923 platform date may describe different structures; the story says so. The brief's status 'gone' is not supported; the FFLA list says Abandoned. The Red Meadow Lake campground is not tied to the lookout site by any source. The 'public' access level is inferred from National Forest land and a public campground, not from a source about the platform site. No photos found.
